subject: 4MB1
skill: Estimate a grouped mean using class midpoints and frequencies.

customQuiz.rationale: Keep the original four-mark M2/M1 + dependent M1 + A1 structure. Numeric and context transformation is not yet calibrated for live use.

requirements: Five fixed unequal-width distance classes (0,2],(2,5],(5,10],(10,20],(20,40] km; five positive integer frequencies sum to 60.
Original walking-club context and generated frequencies; original frequency tuple excluded from fresh generation.
evidenceContract: Only prompt, class table, total, units and maximum marks may be public.
Deep-freeze the package privately before scoring; no live route serves this prototype.
Structured working records five ordered product slots, explicit intention to add, their sum and divisor. A null slot means not shown.
Offline representatives and totals must be half-integers in a bounded domain; other valid notation or methods defer rather than being marked wrong.

constraints: Five frequencies total 60; twice the midpoint product sum is divisible by 6, giving an exact mean with at most two decimal places.

relationships: Midpoints are 1,3.5,7.5,15,30 km; estimate = sum(midpoint times frequency)/60.
Twice the product sum is integral and divisible by 6; the exact mean has at most two decimal places.
First method band is capped at two, not three; division credit requires at least one mark in that band.
difficultyControls: Retain the source total, five rows, unequal class widths and half-integer midpoints. Frequency-size and context changes need demand calibration.

transformations.conditions: Admitted domain only; source-relative demand and response calibration pending.
Needs a separate source and rubric review.

solutionProcedure: Multiply each midpoint by its class frequency, then add the products.
Divide the sum by 60 and report an estimate in km, not a measured exact population mean.

criteria.rule: Non-additive band: M2 for at least three correct midpoint products with intention to add; M1 for at least three within-class representatives (upper endpoint included, lower excluded) in products with addition, OR three correct midpoint products without addition. Unevaluated multiplication allowed.
M1 for dividing their sum by 60, dependent on at least M1 in the preceding band.
A1 for the exact estimated mean or equivalent. The source labels the answer cas, so an answer alone can imply full credit unless obviously obtained incorrectly.

acceptableAlternatives: Exact decimal with optional km, or an exactly equivalent integer fraction, including unreduced forms.
Unevaluated correct product entries in the supported structured working.
Conventional unsupported notation and methods require review; this narrow parser does not define all acceptable exam answers.
dependencies: M2 and M1 in the first band cannot be added.
Division credit requires at least one first-band mark.
All credit can be implied by an exact correct answer alone.
contradictionRules: Additional, crossed-out, wrong-frequency or inconsistent product evidence requires review.
Correct answer with incomplete or different working requires review unless all five midpoint products, addition total and divisor 60 are explicitly correct.
An incorrect addition total may retain method marks; never silently repair it or give final accuracy for a wrong estimate.
A correct equivalent fraction in working with a blank or different final answer requires review because the transcription does not identify the final fraction or subsequent-working intent.

commonErrors.description: Using class boundaries or averaging midpoints without frequencies does not give the correct grouped mean.
Representatives strictly at lower endpoints do not satisfy the source M1 within-class concession.

testPlan: Exhaust the implemented finite frequency domain for arithmetic, determinism and source exclusion. Passing these bounded tests does not establish complete response coverage or assessment calibration.
Check source fixture, all mark totals and dependency boundaries with synthetic response cases; tamper and sparse-input rejection.
Before promotion review AO allocation, numeric/context demand and real learner working; retain unsupported-method review.
